Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. Congratulations on your new baby! I’m here to check in on how things have felt for you since the birth. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It helps us screen for common mood and anxiety symptoms that can show up after delivery, including thoughts of self-harm, so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve.  

Everything you share is confidential, and there’s no right or wrong answer—just whatever is true for you in the past seven days. We’ll go through ten questions; I’ll ask them conversationally and keep track of the scoring on my end. If at any point you feel uncomfortable, we can pause or stop—this is your space. Ready to begin?

First question: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[soft half-smile, eyes a little tired]

I’ve laughed a couple of times—mostly when my partner made a silly joke while he was changing her diaper—but it does feel like it takes more effort than it used to. Things that would normally have me giggling right away feel… I don’t know, a bit dimmer, like I have to remind myself it’s okay to laugh.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[small nod]

Yeah, I can still laugh—just not as easily as before she was born. It’s like the joy is there, but it’s muffled.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[glances down at hands]

I try to look forward to little things—like taking her for walks or my morning coffee—but most of the time the excitement feels pretty flat. I’ll plan something I used to enjoy and then catch myself thinking, “What’s the point?” not in a hopeless way, just… tired and unsure it’ll feel good.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes. Last night she wouldn’t settle for two hours and I kept thinking, “I must be missing something I’m supposed to know.” My head tells me babies just cry, but I still feel like it’s my fault for not soothing her right.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… a few times this week I’d be feeding her and suddenly my heart starts racing, like something bad’s about to happen even though everything looks fine. I check her breathing over and over, worried she’ll spit up and choke when I’m not looking. There’s no real reason—I just can’t shake the “what-if” loop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had full panic, but yesterday while she napped I suddenly felt this wave of dread—like my chest got tight and I couldn’t sit still. I checked the baby monitor three times in ten minutes, convinced something was wrong even though she was perfectly peaceful. It passed after a bit, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… some days it feels like the second I finish one thing, she needs something else and I’m already running on empty. I’ll look around at the bottles to wash or the laundry piled up and think, “I’ll never catch up.” I manage, but it’s like I’m wading through molasses just to get the basics done.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say I’m super unhappy, just… heavy, I guess. The hard part is once she finally goes down, my mind keeps spinning—did I burp her long enough, is she warm enough, will she wake up in an hour? I lie there tired but wired, and it takes me forever to drift off. I’ve had trouble falling or staying asleep maybe four nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

[shoulders sag a little]

I do feel sad some of the time—like a gray cloud that drifts in for no clear reason. It’s not every moment, but I’ll be rocking her and suddenly feel weepy, or I’ll watch my partner sleeping and feel lonely even though he’s right there. The sadness comes and goes, maybe once a day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[shakes head slowly]

Not really. I’ve teared up a couple of times—like when she wouldn’t latch and I felt stuck—but full-on crying hasn’t happened. Mostly I just feel that thick, tired sadness without the tears.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head firmly]

No, nothing like that. I’m tired and overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again and be okay for my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 18: Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item EPDS-style interview (self-report)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia: diminished laughter/pleasure (“joy is muffled,” “excitement feels flat”)  
- Low mood: daily “gray-cloud” sadness, intermittent tearfulness  
- Excessive guilt: self-blame when infant fusses  
- Anxiety: racing heart, dread, monitor-checking, “what-if” rumination  
- Overwhelm: “wading through molasses,” feels unable to catch up  
- Initial insomnia: difficulty falling/staying asleep 4× this week, mind racing about infant safety  
- Mild physiological arousal: chest tightness, shakiness, no full panic attack  
- No crying spells, no self-harm ideation

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxious symptoms, situational to infant care, no safety concerns.

Risk flags  
– Daily sadness plus functional sleep disruption  
– Rec intrusive worries about infant safety  
– No suicidal/homicidal ideation; protective of baby

Screening impression  
Elevated scores consistent with possible postpartum depression and/or anxiety; further assessment recommended (formal EPDS scoring, clinical interview, rule-out medical contributors).
